Senses.PreferredTarget: to gouge healthy flesh and make a wound
SearchAliases: to gouge healthy flesh and make a wound
Senses.Note: The image condemns making a wound where flesh was sound—that is, creating unnecessary trouble by an added move.

Senses.Explanation: The charge literally gouges sound flesh to make a sore, needlessly creating injury or trouble. The cases apply it to lifting a hair, asking permission to pose a question, and Huangbo’s staff. Encounter dialogues and later appraisals consistently use the wound as a criticism of needless addition to an already adequate situation.
